title: APG component store entry
description: ADR 0009 defines the store, ADR 0010 puts its contract on the distribution surface. Two shapes share this document: a package manifest, which sits inside a digest-named directory and covers that directory's bytes exactly, and a service entry, which carries identity only. A record names an identity and never a machine path, because the store root is resolved at use time. A record may also declare which fields of its own health response carry that identity, and what it needs before it is usable - another component, an executable, or the presence of an environment variable.

relativePath.description: Relative, forward-slash separated, and free of '..' segments; the loader enforces the same rule before reading anything.

provenance.description: Where the bytes came from, as acquisition coordinates rather than a location: the component record in scripts/external-components.json is the authority for these values.

digest.description: sha256 over the canonical form of this manifest without the digest field, which is why the manifest is excluded from its own file set.

endpoint.description: A loopback address and port. Runtime additionally checks IP validity and port <= 65535. localhost is mapped to 127.0.0.1 without DNS; remote destinations are not supported.

health.description: A percent-encoded read-only path (optional query), no fragment, authority or control characters. One bounded GET, no redirects.

revision.description: The revision the project pinned. Without it the identity of whatever answers cannot be verified, and discovery reports degraded rather than available.

singleton.description: A singleton with two live instances is a conflict, never a choice.

delivery.description: An already-running service cannot be downloaded, so a service entry can never be fetched.

identity.description: Which fields of the health response carry the identity, when they are not `id` and `revision`. Measured need: a real service answered with `service`/`rev`, and a probe that could only read `id`/`revision` could never mark it available.

asserted_identity.description: The record admits that no read-only request can check who answers - an identity provable only through a handshake the store does not perform. Such a service can be reachable but is never available: it stays degraded. Mutually exclusive with identity.

stop.description: How this service actually stops. Measured need: one component's watcher prints a graceful-shutdown line and never exits, so the Operator contract must not assume SIGTERM is enough.

requirement.description: One thing a component needs before it is usable. A single-key object, so that a component requirement can never be confused with an executable or a variable of the same name.

component.description: An id whose final verdict, including all transitive prerequisites, must be available. Cycles and unprobed service health are not satisfied. probe verifies required packages only; verify never probes services.

bin.description: An executable that must be on PATH and executable.

env.description: An environment variable that must be set. Presence only: the store never reads, compares or records its value.

requires.description: Declared prerequisites. An entry with an unmet requirement is degraded, never available, and the verdict names which requirement failed.
